subject: Deployment load carving and SLA validation — clarification and runbook
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika@stratos-systems.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stratos-systems.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Performance questionnaire — baseline & scaling clarifications

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the RFP response so far. Our architects have a few follow-ups specific to benchmarking and SLA validation before we finalize the scope:

1) Test harness: are you able to provide the exact harness you use for published numbers (load generator, request shaping, seed prompts)?
2) Warm-up behavior: how long should a run be to reach steady-state (KV cache warm-up, JIT/compilation effects)?
3) Burst handling: what happens when sustained peak QPS jumps 3x for 60s — does the system shed, queue, or elastically scale?
4) Measurement windows: for latency SLOs do you report p50/p90/p99 over 1s, 10s, 5m windows?
5) Resource mapping: for our expected mix (chat sessions with avg 280 tokens, 30% function/tool calls), what GPU counts / model variants do you recommend for a 99.99% uptime SLA?

We'd like to schedule a short technical run-through next week and review your runbook and any sample traces. Could you attach the runbook and any scripts you typically run?

Best,
Anika
Anika Shah
Head of Platform Engineering — Stratos Systems

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@stratos-systems.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance questionnaire — baseline & scaling clarifications

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear questions. Attaching our public runbook (redwood-benchmark-runbook-v1.pdf) and a short notes file. High level answers below; Vivek will follow up with the detailed harness and configs.

- Test harness: we use an open-source load driver (customized Gatling+Python harness) with traffic shaping based on recorded production traces. We include seed prompts + randomized user histories to simulate KV cache effects.
- Warm-up: warm-up varies by model size; empirically we see KV cache stabilization at ~900–1,500 warm-up requests per GPU for typical chat workloads. We recommend 20–30 minutes for long-run steady-state on larger sequence lengths.
- Burst handling: policy depends on deployment: Hosted favors graceful degradation with burst credits and autoscale; Dedicated can be configured to queue vs reject—default is queue up to 30s then shed.
- Measurement: our internal reports provide p50/p90/p95/p99 over 1m and 5m rolling windows; for RFPs we can also supply 10s windows for spike sensitivity.
- Resource mapping: we'll propose a recommended baseline after Vivek's sizing exercise, but expect ~1–1.5 tokens/sec per A100 GPU-core for some quantized variants; exact numbers depend on quantization and batching.

Proposed next steps: Vivek and Karthik will prepare a runbook extract and a small load package (scripts + sample trace) by EOD Thu. Can you share the time slots you have next week for a 60-min run-through?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-benchmark-runbook-v1.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@stratos-systems.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed test harness & measurement plan (draft)

Anika / team — putting the draft harness and measurement plan here so you can comment. I'm attaching the load scripts and a minimal kv-cache config. Key points:

1) Harness components (attached):
   - load-scripts-v2.tar.gz (driver, sample prompts, shapefiles)
   - sample_trace.json (10k-record synthetic trace to reproduce session mix)
   - kv-cache-config.yaml (prefix caching policies we enable for repeated prompts)

2) Run patterns:
   - Steady-state run: 45 minutes at target QPS, with a 10-minute warm-up period and 5-minute cooldown.
   - Spike test: 3x QPS for 60s repeated 4x with 3 minute recovery windows to observe overload/backpressure.
   - Soak test: 6 hours at 60–70% of peak expected QPS to measure long-tail memory growth and token accounting.

3) Metrics to capture (per-second granularity):
   - Request QPS, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, host CPU, memory, queue depth
   - Latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9) with context of token count and function calls
   - KV cache hit rate, cold-start fraction, and per-request token breakdown

4) Acceptance criteria proposal for RFP:
   - p95 < 250ms for prompt+first-token for chat with <=512 tokens in steady-state
   - p99 < 450ms over 5m window
   - Throughput: sustain N tokens/sec per allocation (we'll provide exact numbers for the model variant you select)
   - Failure mode: under sustained 3x bursts we degrade to queued requests for up to 30s, then best-effort shedding if queue thresholds exceeded

5) Test environment notes:
   - Use isolated Dedicated pool when benchmarking for reproducibility (no noisy neighbors)
   - Ensure same model artifact (commit hash) and quantization flags are pinned across runs
   - Record hardware telemetry and exporter traces (Prometheus + OpenTelemetry) so results are auditable

I'll drop the artifacts in the Drive link and can run an internal smoke test in our staging cluster. Feedback welcome.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: load-scripts-v2.tar.gz, kv-cache-config.yaml

From: BenchmarkLabs <eng@benchmarklabs.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Shah <anika@stratos-systems.com>, procurement@stratos-systems.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed test harness & measurement plan (draft)

Thanks for the draft Vivek — this is helpful. A couple of technical clarifications before we schedule the run: 

- Traffic shaping: when you say "production traces" can you surface a redacted example trace with timing and token counts (we only need ~1k lines) so we can validate our driver reproduces the tail behavior?
- Warm-up definition: you reference warm-up requests per GPU; is that measured against unique session prefixes or total requests? That changes warm-up length for session-heavy apps.
- Autoscale/elasticity: for Dedicated pools can you provide the autoscale smoothing/window settings used in your tests (scale-up threshold, scale-down cooldown)?
- Observability: we need a mapping from metric names in your run to the RFP table (exact label names) so we can automate ingestion.

Also, can you confirm whether your acceptance criteria allow for a fallback model (smaller quantized variant) during overload, or does the contract expect identical model outputs during SLA periods?

If you can attach a 1k-line sample_trace.json and the metric->label map, we'll replicate on our side and propose three time slots next week.

—BenchmarkLabs Eng
eng@benchmarklabs.io

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: BenchmarkLabs <eng@benchmarklabs.io>, Anika Shah <anika@stratos-systems.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed test harness & measurement plan (draft) — artifacts + schedule

Thanks — attaching the 1k-line sample_trace.json to the Drive link and the metric name map. Short answers inline: 

- Redacted trace: shared at https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b-redwood-runbook (sample_trace.json in /artifacts).
- Warm-up: we measure warm-up as unique session prefix population (so number of unique prefixes matters). We will annotate the trace to flag repeats.
- Autoscale config: our Dedicated default test profile uses scale-up threshold = 75% GPU utilization sustained for 45s; scale-down cooldown = 180s. We'll include the exact policy YAML.
- Fallback model: for the RFP baseline we recommend identical model outputs; fallback to a smaller quantized variant is acceptable for the "best-effort" policy but must be disclosed and documented in acceptance criteria. If Stratos requires invariant outputs, we will lock to a non-fallback policy for the run.

Proposed acceptance criteria (final): p95 < 250ms steady-state (512-token prompts), p99 < 450ms over any 5m window; documented degradation policy for bursts >3x lasting >30s.

Available time slots for a 60-min run-through: Tue 12/1 09:00–10:00 PT, Wed 12/2 14:00–15:00 PT, Thu 12/3 11:00–12:00 PT. Please pick one and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — happy to run the initial smoke test in staging prior to the joint run.

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
